title: M/S. Toshniwal Brothers (Sr) Pvt. Ltd vs M/S. Sri Sidhi Chemicals on 5 September, 2015
full_text: M/S. Toshniwal Brothers (Sr) Pvt. Ltd vs M/S. Sri Sidhi Chemicals on 5 September, 2015 IN THE COURT OF THE XXVII ADDL. CHIEF METROPOLITON MAGISTRATE, NRUPATHUNGA ROAD, BENGALURU CITY. Dated this the 5th day of September-2015 :: PRESENT :: SRI. MALLANAGOUDA, B.Com., LL.B., XXVII Addl. C.M.M., Bengaluru City. C.C. NO. 31529/2014 & C.C. NO. 31367/2014 COMPLAINANT: M/s. Toshniwal Brothers (SR) Pvt. Ltd., Regd Office : No.11, AECS Layout, 1st Stage, Geddalahalli, Sanjaya Nagar, Bangalore - 560 094. By Chairman, Represented by its Authorized, Representative & Authorized Signatory Sri. A.B. Badrinath. (Rept. by Sri. Sitarama. G. Hegde. Adv.) V/S ACCUSED: 1. M/s. Sri Sidhi Chemicals, No.45, 3rd Cross, 9th 'A' Main, Mathikere, Bangalore - 560 054. Common Judgment 2 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 2. Smt. P. Pushpa, (Pushpavathi), Managing Partner, M/s. Sri Sidhi Chemicals, No.45, 3rd Cross, 9th 'A' Main, Mathikere, Bangalore - 560 054. 3. Sri. B.K. Rudresh, Managing Partner, M/s. Sri Sidhi Chemicals, No.3/1, (New No.799), 6th Cross, 3rd Main, Prakashnagar, Bangalore - 560 021. 4. Sri. Rajesh, Managing Partner, M/s. Sri Sidhi Chemicals, U-51, 3rd Cross, Pipeline Road, Malleshwaram, Bangalore - 560 003. (Rept. by Sri. S.S. Hiremath. Adv.) OFFENCE COMPLAINED OF : U/Sec. 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act . PLEAD OF THE ACCUSED : Not guilty. FINAL ORDER : Accused No.4 is convicted DATE OF ORDER : 05-09-2015 (MALLANAGOUDA) XXVII Addl.CMM., Bengaluru. *** Common Judgment 3 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 :: COMMON JUDGMENT :: Since the complainant and accused persons in both the cases are one and the same, it is decided to write common judgement in respect of both the cases. 2. In both the cases complainant has filed the complaint against the accused persons under Section.200 Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 3. The brief facts of the complainant's case in all the cases are as under: The complainant is a private limited company doing business of Commission Agent of Goa Glass Fibre Limited and collect the amount of the goods supplied. Accused No.1 is the partnership firm, accused No.2 to 4 are the Managing Partners of accused No.1 firm. On the basis of purchase order placed by the accused persons, complainant has made arrangements for supply of materials on different dates and Common Judgment 4 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 paid the value of the materials to Goa Glass Fibre Ltd., to pay the value of the materials purchased by them, accused persons have issued cheques bearing Nos.135452, 135451, 135453 and 135454, all dated: 04-09-2014 for Rs.2,88,611/-, Rs.2,71,320/-, Rs.2,00,511/- and Rs.1,93,102/- respectively, all the cheques are drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Gokula Branch, Bangalore-54, but when complainant has presented those cheques to bank for encashment the same have been dishonoured and returned with an endorsement as 'Funds Insufficient", after dishonour of the cheques complainant got issued legal notice dated: 25-09-2014 to accused person, inspite of service of notice also accused persons have not paid the cheques amount to complainant. Therefore the accused persons have committed the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 4. The complainant has filed complaint in C.C.31529/2014 for dishonour of cheque Nos:135452 and Common Judgment 5 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 135451 and C.C.31367/2014 for dishonour of cheque Nos. 135453 and 135454. 5. After service of summons, accused No.2 to 4 have appeared before this court and pleaded not guilty for the offence under Section.138 Negotiable Instruments Act. However, when matter was posted for evidence accused No.2 and 3 have got the matter compromised and accused No.4 alone has contested the cases. Hence, the trial has been conducted against him for the said offence. 6. On the basis of the above facts, following points have arisen for my consideration: POINTS 1. Whether complainant proves beyond reasonable doubt that to pay the value of the materials purchased from complainant company, accused persons have issued cheques bearing Nos.135452, 135451, 135453 and 135454, all dated: 04-09-2014 for Rs.2,88,611/-, Rs.2,71,320/-, Rs.2,00,511/- and Rs.1,93,102/- respectively, all the cheques are drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Gokula Branch, Bangalore- 54, but on presentation the said cheques are Common Judgment 6 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 dishonoured and returned with an endorsement as "Funds Insufficient", after that complainant got issued legal notice dated: 25-09-2014 to accused persons, even after issuance of notice also accused persons have failed to pay the amount involved in the cheques. Thereby the accused persons are liable for conviction for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act? 2. What order? 7. In support of its case, complainant company examined one witness in both the cases as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Exs.P1 to P21 in C.C.31529/2014 and C.C.31366/2014 and Ex.P1 to P23 in C.C.31367/2014 on its behalf. On the other hand accused has not produced any oral evidence but he got marked portion of complaint as Ex.D1 on his behalf. 8. Heard arguments. 9. My findings on the above points are as under: Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: As per final order, for the following: Common Judgment 7 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 REASONS 10. POINT NO.1: It is the case of the complainant that accused No.1 is the partnership firm, to which accused No.2 to 4 are the partners, they used to purchase Glass Fibre and other materials from Goa Glass Fibre Ltd., through the complainant on credit basis and to pay the amount due infavour of complainant company, accused have issued 4 (four) cheques all dated: 04-09-2014 for different amount drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Gokula Branch, Bangalore- 54, but when complainant has presented those cheques to bank, same are dishonoured with endorsement as 'Funds Insufficient', after that complainant got issued legal notice dated: 25-09-2014, Inspite of service of notice also accused have not paid the amount involved in the cheques. Thereby the accused have committed an offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 11. During evidence P.W.1 namely A.B. Badrinath has filed his affidavit as chief-examination in which he once Common Judgment 8 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 again restated the facts alleged in the complaints as discussed above. In cross-examination he deposed that at the time of supplying the goods only accused persons have issued cheques, after about 5 to 6 months they informed the complainant to present the cheques to bank, he denied suggestions regarding issuance of blank cheques, he admitted suggestions stating that the accused No.4 has not signed on the cheques. 12. The complainant has produced documents like cheques, bank endorsements etc. 13. During arguments learned counsel for complainant has argued that when there is no dispute about existence of legally dischargeable debt and accused persons have admitted that the cheques in question are belongs to accused No.4 firm and accused No.4 is admittedly the managing partner of the accused No.1 firm, therefore accused No.4 is also vicariously liable for the acts done by the other partners of Common Judgment 9 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 the firm. Therefore when cheques are dishonoured for want of funds and after dishonour of the cheques complainant has complied all other conditions of Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Therefore, accused No.4 is liable for conviction. In support of his said arguments, he has relied upon the following judgements: ILR 2014 KAR 2168 CREF Finance Limited, Kolkata V/s. Sree Shanthi Homes Private Limited, Bangalore & Anr. (a) The Board of Directors of the Company collectively entitled to exercise the powers and to do the acts on behalf of the Company. Section.291 of the Companies Act confers the authority to the Board of Directors collectively. Therefore, if a complaint is to be filed, it is necessary for the Board of Directors to authorize any person to file a complaint or depose to the facts in a case and such an authority could be granted by the Board of Directors only under a Resolution. (b) Company is a juristic person and any person on behalf of the Company has to be authorized by the Company under Articles of Association or by a separate Resolution to depose on behalf of the Company. *** Common Judgment 10 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 ILR 2003 KAR 4617 M/s. Prudential Engineers and Others V/s. Kuskoor Bharath Ram (A) Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (Central Act No.29 of 1881) - Section.138 , 141 - Indian Partnership Act - Section.25 - Code of Criminal Procedure , 1973 (Act No.2/1974) - Section.482 - Offence under Section.138 to 142 of N.I. Act - Complaint filed against partnership firm and its partners - Should the complaint be proceeded with against the partners. Held - complainant being a stranger to the company, firm or association of individuals, will not be in a position to know the management or internal affairs or arrangements of such company, firm or association of individuals for the conduct of its business at the time of transaction. So, when legal notice was issued, as required under law, it will be for the persons, who were issued/served with such notice, to make it clear not only that they were not in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business of the company, firm or association of individuals, but also to come out specifying the person (s) in charge of and responsible for the consequently in the circumstances all o them are arrayed as accused, they cannot subsequently contend that they were not liable to be proceeded impleaded as accused. Of course, from reply notice, if it can be made out or clear that any one or more among such persons only is/are liable to be prosecuted and proceeded with and such other person(s) also take up to the liability for self and also for and on behalf of the company/firm/association of Common Judgment 11 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 individuals, then such other person(s) only to be proceeded with an not any other person(s) even if persons happens to be director(s) or partner(s) or officer(s) of such company, firm or association of individuals. So also, if the liability under the cheque is disputed or in dispute or not made clear or not admitted and taken by any body and for that, evidence is required, then all persons can be proceeded with/prosecuted. When the complainant has impleaded all the partners with firm as accused, no fault can be found with it, as he was not at fault nor wrong in impleaded all the partners as accused, keeping in mind Section.25 of the Partnership Act. That being so, taking cognizance and issuing process against all the partners of the firm also by the Trial Court was not at all bad in law. *** 1992 AIR SCW 72 Sanganer Dal and Flour Mill V/s. F.C.I. and others. (A) Arbitration Act (10 of 1940), S.20 - Powers of Court - Contract entered into by one of partners of firm - Not repudiated as per Law by other partners - Contract is valid - Presence of arbitration clause in contract - Reference under S.20 by court to arbitration - Not without jurisdiction. *** 2009 Cri.L.J. 224 Suresh Kallappa Makavi Common Judgment 12 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 V/s. Madan Bindurao Desai & Anr. (A) Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881), Ss.138, 142 - Cheque dishonour proceedings - Can be initiated as against a person who has signed cheque - Cheque of a joint account signed by two persons - Complainant can choose and either proceed against both signatories or proceed against one of signatories or proceed against one of signatories - Complainant cannot be compelled to proceed against both signatories - Very fact that petitioner/accused having signed cheque - Would establish that the petitioner/accused was also an active partner responsible for the day to day affairs of the accused company - Contention of the petitioner/accused that he was a sleeping partner of the firm not tenable. *** 2006(3) KCCR 1948 M/s. S.T.P. Limited V/s. M/s. Usha Paints and Decorators and Another (A) Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881- Section.138 - The distinction between issuance of cheque for repayment of debt and issuance of cheque as a security for repayment of debt is illusory in law - Any cheque, whether issued towards repayment of debt or liability, or as a security, if dishonoured, the drawer of a cheque incurs liability of prosecution under Section. 138 of the N.I. Act . *** Common Judgment 13 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 AIR 2002 S.C.3014 I.C.D.S. Ltd., V/s. Beemna Shabeer and Anr. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) - Section.138 - Dishonour of cheque - Key expressions any cheque and other liability in S.138 - Clarifies the legislative intent - Issue regarding co-extensive liability of guarantor and principal debtor - Is totally out of purview of S.138 - Cheque issued by guarantor - Cannot be said to have not been issued for purpose of discharging any debt or liability - Complaint under S.138 for its dishonour - Maintainable. *** AIR 2010 S.C.1898 Rangappa V/s. Mohan (A) Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) - Section.138 - Dishonour of cheque - On account of 'stop payment' instructions sent by accused to Bank in respect of post dated cheque - S.138 is attracted - Insufficient of funds in account, irrespective. (B) Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881), S.138 - Existence of legally recoverable debt or liability - Is matter of presumption. *** Common Judgment 14 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 14. On the other counsel for accused has argued that as accused No.4 was not attending day to day affairs of the partnership firm and he is not the signatory of the cheques, accused No.4 is not liable for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. In support of his said arguments he has relied upon the following judgment: (2010) 2 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 1113 National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. V/s. Harmeet Singh Paintal and Anr. (C) Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881- Sections.141, 138 and 142 - Dishonour of cheque - Offence by company - Vicarious liability of Director/Managing Director/Joint Director - Averments required to be made in complaint - In case of a Director, held, complaint should specifically spell out how and in what manner the Director was in charge of or was responsible to the accused company for conduct of its business - Mere bald statement that he was in charge of and was responsible to that every Director knows about the transaction - In the absence of specific averment as to the role of co-accused Director, trial court's order summoning him, rightly quashed by High Court - However, where the accused is the Managing Director or a Joint/Managing Director or a Director who had signed the cheque on behalf of Common Judgment 15 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 the accused company, making of such specific averment, held, not necessary. *** 15. On perusal of evidence produced by the complainant and arguments of both the counsels it appears that regarding existence of legally dischargeable debt is concerned, complainant has produced copies of invoices and accused No.4 has not seriously disputed the said invoices which shows that the contention of complainant that accused No.1 firm has purchased materials through complainant company on credit basis and as on the dates of the cheques accused No.1 firm was liable to pay the amount mentioned in the cheques is true. Regarding issuance of cheques for payment of amount or otherwise is concerned as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in judgment reported in AIR - 2010 S.C.1898, as per Section.139 of N.I. Act, if cheque is admittedly of the accused, it is necessary to presume that the accused has issued the said cheques for payment of legally dischargeable debt and burden lies on the accused to rebut the presumption, but here in this case accused No.4 has not Common Judgment 16 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 at all brought anything on record from the mouth of P.W.1 or he has not produced any evidence to rebut the presumption, therefore it appears that as on the dates mentioned in the cheques accused No.1 firm was liable to pay the amount mentioned in the cheques and for payment of the said amount only accused No.2 and 3 who are the authorized signatories of the accused No.1 firm have issued the cheques in question in all these cases. 16. Regarding contention of the accused No.4 that merely because accused No.4 is the partner of the firm, he is not liable for punishment, by looking to complaints it appears that the accused No.4 is described as Managing Partner and accused No.4 has not at all disputed the same. In judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for accused No.4 reported in (2010)2 S.C.C. (Cri). 1113, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that in case of a Director or Partner complaint should specifically spell out how and in what manner the Director or Partner was in charge of or was Common Judgment 17 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 responsible to the accused company or firm for conduct of its business, but as held in said judgment itself if the accused is the managing director or managing partner of the company or firm, it is not necessary to make such specific averments in the complaint, accused No.4 has not disputed the descriptions of the complaint describing the accused No.4 as Managing Partner, therefore it appears that though there is no specific averments in the complaint regarding the manner in which accused No.4 was involved in the day to day affairs of the accused No.1 firm, since accused No.4 is the Managing Partner, he is also liable for issuance of cheques in favour of the complainant company without there being sufficient funds in the bank account of the accused No.1 firm, therefore when there is evidence about existence of legally dischargeable debt, issuance of cheques for payment of amount due infavour of the complainant and accused No.4 is the managing partner of the accused No.1 firm, but on presentation of cheques, the same are dishonoured, after that complainant has complied all other Common Judgment 18 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 conditions of Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, therefore definitely accused No.4 is liable for punishment for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. However, by considering the peculiar circumstances of the case, it is decided to impose fine only to the extent of amount of the cheques but not to send the accused to prison. Hence, I answered Point No.1 in Affirmative. 17. POINT NO.2: In view of my findings on Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER Acting under Section.265 of Cr.P.C., accused in both the three cases i.e., C.C.31529 and C.C.31366 is convicted for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Accused shall pay fine of Rs.5,59,931/- in C.C.31529/2014 and Rs.3,93,613/- in C.C.31367/2014. Out of the fine amount Common Judgment 19 C.C.31529 & 31367/2014 Rs.5,000/- in each case is ordered to be remitted to the State and remaining amount is ordered to be paid to the complainant as compensation. Office is directed to keep the copy of judgment in all the four cases. (Dictated to Stenographer, transcribed and computerized by him, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 5th day of September-2015.) (MALLANA GOUDA) XXVII Addl.
